messages.author: 9cd2f7a3e99756cd
messages.subject: Estimators in SEM
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am a bit confused regarding the estimator choice when developing a SEM mode.

Specifically, I can't decide between the WLSMV and MLR/MLM options. My data are non-normal and the dependent variable is a latent variable with continuous indicators. The IVs include two latent variables, one with binary categorical and one with continuous indicators. What is not clear to me is if the estimator should account for categorical data when they are present in the model or only when they are dependent.

I also read that WLS approcahes are not recommended for small sample sizes, but having a sample of 1500 I think I could also try this.

Any suggestions? Some references would be really appreciated.

Many thanks in advance

messages.author: 5b9c62b1c7cbc1e6
messages.subject: Re: Estimators in SEM
parts:
Andy,

If the indicators of your IV are latent, they are endogenous, so DWLS/WLSMV.

An 1,500 is not large for purposes of WLS. Think more like 5,000.

Pat

Hi Pat,

Thank you very much for your quick reply.

Just to confirm, if my model is the following, latent variables lat2 and lat3 are considered endogenous even if there is not an arrow pointing at them in the path analysis, as usually described in literature?:

mod_sem <- '
#measurements
lat1 =~ y1 + y2
lat2 =~ x1  + x2
lat3=~ x3 + x4+ x5

lat1 ~ lat2 + lat3 + x6
'

Lastly, would my sample size be considered appropriate for DWLS/WLSMV even if it is not large for WLS?

messages.author: 5b9c62b1c7cbc1e6
messages.subject: Re: Estimators in SEM
parts:
Not quite.

lat2 and lat3 are exogenous and continuous.

But x1 through x5 are endogenous. So if one of those is binary, which is how I read your post, that drives the choice of estimator.

Pat
